title: At the Edge of the Heart: ULP FPGA-Based CNN for On-Device Cardiac Feature Extraction in Smart Health Sensors for Astronauts
authors: Kazi Mohammad Abidur Rahman, Davis Rakhshan, Philipp Lütke, Laura Harms
key_finding_quote: Demonstrates real-time Seismocardiography (SCG) cardiac feature extraction directly on an ultra-low-power wearable FPGA (Lattice iCE40UP5K) using quantized neural networks for resource-constrained astronaut health sensors.

title: Space Physiology and Technology: Musculoskeletal Adaptations, Countermeasures, and Opportunities for Wearable Systems
authors: Shamas Ul Ebad Khan, Rejin John Varghese, Panagiotis Kassanos, Dario Farina
key_finding_quote: Links wearable physiological and biomechanical telemetry directly to closed-loop exercise countermeasures (ARED resistive loading) to mitigate microgravity bone and muscle loss.

title: Modeling Considerations for Developing Deep Space Autonomous Spacecraft and Simulators
authors: Christopher Agia, Guillem Casadesus Vila, Saptarshi Bandyopadhyay, David S. Bayard (JPL / Caltech)
key_finding_quote: Defines System-Level Autonomy: autonomous software that jointly reasons across multiple interconnected subsystems (e.g., spacecraft ECLSS environment + crew health) to resolve conflicting single-sensor information.

title: Spacecraft Anomaly Detection with Attention Temporal Convolution Network
authors: Liang Liu, Ling Tian, Zhao Kang, Tianqi Wan
key_finding_quote: Shows that single-variable domain thresholding fails in complex spacecraft telemetry due to cross-variable correlations, motivating multi-parameter context-aware anomaly detection.

title: A Comparison of Deep Learning Architectures for Spacecraft Anomaly Detection
key_finding_quote: Benchmarks lightweight time-series anomaly detection architectures for early fault and hazard identification in critical spacecraft operations.

title: Operations for Autonomous Spacecraft
authors: Rebecca Castano, Tiago Vaquero, Federico Rossi, Vandi Verma (JPL)
key_finding_quote: Establishes onboard content-based data summarization and autonomous decision workflows for deep-space missions operating under severe communication latency.

title: NSIDDx: A Design Framework for Neuro-Symbolic, Practitioner-First Differential Diagnosis in Low-Resource Settings
key_finding_quote: Demonstrates that open-ended LLM+RAG pipelines produce unverifiable outputs on uncommon clinical presentations, whereas a Neuro-Symbolic pipeline (combining deterministic clinical rules with RAG) ensures verifiable differential diagnosis in isolated settings.

title: Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Causality Assessment (MARCA) of Individual Case Safety Reports in Pharmacovigilance
authors: Daisy Rae Lopez, Angela Boccia, Maurizio Sessa
key_finding_quote: Validates a multi-agent RAG architecture combining literature retrieval, drug-label/contraindication assessment, and objective clinical evidence.

title: Unanimously Wrong: Certified Abstention from How Medical LLM Consensus Forms
authors: Xiaoyang Wang, Tianrui Wang, Christopher C. Yang
key_finding_quote: Proves why medical AI systems must track diagnostic confidence and fall back to verified deterministic checklists rather than relying on ungrounded LLM generation.

title: ClinAgent: A ReAct-Based Agent for Conversational Access to Clinical Trial Information
authors: Antonino Vaccarella, Riccardo Cantini, Domenico Talia, Paolo Trunfio
key_finding_quote: Demonstrates an agentic ReAct RAG workflow for synthesizing structured clinical databases into grounded, multi-turn decision support.

title: Crewed Missions to Mars: Modeling the Impact of Astrophysical Charged Particles on Astronauts and Their Health
authors: Dimitra Atri, Caitlin MacArthur, Sriram Devata, Konstantin Herbst
project_layer: Layer 1 & Layer 2 (Mars Solar Radiation & ARS Modeling)
key_finding_quote: Models Galactic Cosmic Ray (GCR) and Solar Particle Event (SPE) organ doses during Mars transit and surface operations, quantifying Acute Radiation Syndrome (ARS) risks.

title: Modeling the effectiveness of radiation shielding materials for astronaut protection on Mars
key_finding_quote: Quantifies radiation dose attenuation across spacecraft and habitat shielding materials to keep crew exposure below Space Permissible Exposure Limits.

title: Limitations in Predicting the Space Radiation Health Risk for Exploration Astronauts
authors: Jeffery C. Chancellor, Rebecca S. Blue, Keith A. Cengel, Serena M. Auñón-Chancellor
key_finding_quote: Co-authored by NASA Astronaut Physician Dr. Serena Auñón-Chancellor; highlights the clinical necessity of continuous in-flight biodosimetry and hematological monitoring during deep-space exploration.

title: Evaluating the Effects of Situated and Embedded Visualisation in Augmented Reality Guidance for Isolated Medical Assistance
authors: Frederick George Vickery, Sébastien Kubicki, Charlotte Hoareau, Lucas Brand
key_finding_quote: Demonstrates that isolated operators performing complex medical diagnosis and treatment require situated, low-friction visual checklists to maintain autonomy and prevent cognitive overload.

title: Beyond LunAR: An augmented reality UI for deep-space exploration missions
authors: Sarah Radway, Anthony Luo, Carmine Elvezio, Jenny Cha
key_finding_quote: Contrasts the 2.6-second Lunar round-trip communication delay with the 22-minute Mars delay, establishing UI design rules for astronaut autonomy independent of Earth-based assistance.
